definitions.explanation: The sound made by an animal, bird, or insect. Covers all animal vocalizations from chirping to roaring.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鳴|な}き{声|ごえ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: I can hear a dog barking.
At night, the chirping of insects echoes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{色々|いろいろ}→色々：02352_iroiro⟧な⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鳴|な}き{声|ごえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{間近|まぢか}→間近：14527_majika⟧で⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: At the zoo, you can hear various animal cries up close.

notes:
USAGE:
Used for sounds made by animals, birds, and insects. Not used for human voices (that would be {泣|な}き{声|ごえ}, meaning crying voice, using a different kanji for なき).

NOTE ON KANJI:
⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧ (animal sounds) vs. ⟦{泣|な}く→泣く：00655_naku⟧ (human crying). The kanji {鳴|な} is specifically for animal vocalizations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鳴|な}き{声|ごえ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧ (to hear animal cries)
- ⟦{鳥|とり}→鳥：00679_tori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鳴|な}き{声|ごえ} (birdsong)
- ⟦{虫|むし}→虫：02262_mushi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鳴|な}き{声|ごえ} (chirping of insects)
